assessments.reasoning: In §10.1.8.1 step 1 obtains the own descriptor through O.[[GetOwnProperty]]. Steps 3–5 reach the accessor branch and extract [[Get]]. Step 6 returns undefined when that field is undefined. Step 7 supplies Receiver as the second argument to Call. §7.3.13 defines this argument as the this value passed to the callable object's [[Call]].

challenge.method: Traced the descriptor-absent, data-descriptor, getter-absent and getter-present paths with a Receiver distinct from O. Compared the call arguments with §7.3.13 and the separate Get helper in §7.3.2.
challenge.results: The absent-descriptor path consults the prototype and forwards Receiver when it delegates. The data-descriptor path reads [[Value]]. The accessor path keeps Receiver even when it differs from O. §7.3.2 supplies O when that helper initiates a read, which is a separate choice at the call site.

limitations: The conclusion concerns the this argument passed into [[Call]]. The function's own this-binding semantics govern what its body observes, and its call can complete abruptly.
